**Approx. 154,518 actual miles** (see gauge cluster note below).

5.7L LT1 V8
Automatic transmission
T-Tops

Warbird hood
NGK spark plugs
98-02 style taillights
Apple CarPlay & Android Auto
Backup camera
Morimoto LED fog lights
LED interior/exterior lighting
Aftermarket wheels with Nexen tires
1997 Firebird/Trans Am gauge cluster with LED backlighting

Front/rear drilled & slotted brakes, pads & calipers
Transmission service
Coolant service
Rear brake lines

**$9,999 OBO. No trades.**

The beautiful Red sport seats create a premium and distinctive environment, while premium materials and meticulous craftsmanship surround every occupant. Equipped with Air Lift system to eliminate the vehicle squat when towing heavy loads. Bags hold up to 100 psi.

New rims and tires as of 2019(thereabout).

Headrests used to have screens in them for passengers (kids) to watch movies. System got kicked around and was removed (obsolete tech). Back side of headrests can be covered but that hasn't happened yet.
Paint is sunburnt.
Interior is good to better than good.
Small crinkle in passenger side body behind passenger door. May not be noticeable in pictures.
Moon roof sometimes loses its seal when driving and you have to punch the button to reestablish the seal.
DIN box needs to be figured out but it does connect to Bluetooth.
Original paint was blue on the top and white on the bottom with an orange swoosh (ugly). Truck sat in my driveway for years and the new paint burnt.

2 owners.
As I was told, the first was a woman who owned a concrete company in Texas and used it as her personal job site vehicle.
Next owner (my trust) never used the truck other than to and from our ranch located in Wyoming. No heavy hauling and very little hauling if any. Mostly highway miles.

The base turbo four-cylinder feels sprightly around town, but the Macan really comes alive with the twin-turbo 2.9-liter V-6powered S model. Quickness is important in a crossover with sporting intentions, but we wouldn't be nearly as impressed with the Macan if it weren't for its all-around competence on the road. It feels remarkably like a sports sedan, and the 7-speed dual-clutch automatic delivers rapid shifts worthy of the chassis and turbocharged engines. The ride is wonderfully damped and carefully controlled, and it's rare for a jolt from the pavement to throw the Macan off course. The steering is a tad lighter than it is in Porsche's sports cars, but it's still micrometer-accurate and pleasantly tactile. At our test track, the base turbo four-cylinder Macan bounds to 60 mph in just 5.0 seconds. The Macan S is significantly quicker, hitting the 60-mph mark in just 3.8 seconds, trailing the more powerful GTS by only 0.3 seconds; it leaves both the Audi SQ5 and the Jaguar F-Pace S behind as well.
